title: Implementing a deque with a doubly linked list
summary: References to the head and tail and links in both directions allow insertion and removal at either end without moving intermediate nodes.
context: The deque is on the left and its vertical doubly linked list on the right. Both run from front to rear, top to bottom. The head is the front and the tail is the rear. Between neighboring nodes, next points down and prev points up.
description: Five frames show the initial state, appending 4, prepending 1, removing 4 from the rear, and removing 1 from the front. The new 4 is cyan and 1 is orange. The original elements 3, 2, and 5 stay in place.
result: With references to both the head and tail, removing the last element reaches the new tail directly via the old tail's prev link. There is no need to traverse from the head. Insertion and removal at either end update only nearby references and take O(1) time.

frames.title: Initial deque
frames.explanation: The list starts as 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5. The head is 3 and the tail is 5, giving the deque [3, 2, 5] on the left. There is no return value.
frames.announcement: Initial list: 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 3 and tail 5.

frames.title: Add 4 at the rear
frames.explanation: Call push_last(4). Attach new node 4 below 5. Set 5.next to 4 and 4.prev to 5. The list is now 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5 ⇄ 4. The head is still 3 and the new tail is 4. No value is returned.
frames.announcement: Link 5 and 4 in both directions and update the tail reference to 4.

frames.title: Add 1 at the front
frames.explanation: Call push_first(1). Attach new node 1 above 3. Set 1.next to 3 and 3.prev to 1. The list is now 1 ⇄ 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5 ⇄ 4. The new head is 1 and the tail is still 4. No value is returned.
frames.announcement: Link 1 and 3 in both directions and update the head reference to 1.

frames.title: Remove 4 from the rear
frames.explanation: Call pop_last(). Follow 4.prev directly to 5 and set the tail reference to 5. Disconnect the links between 5 and 4 and return 4. The list is now 1 ⇄ 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 1 and tail 5.
frames.announcement: Follow 4.prev to 5 and make it the tail. Detach node 4 and return 4.

frames.title: Remove 1 from the front
frames.explanation: Call pop_first(). Follow 1.next to 3 and set the head reference to 3. Disconnect the links between 1 and 3 and return 1. The list is back to 3 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5, with head 3 and tail 5.
frames.announcement: Follow 1.next to 3 and make it the head. Detach node 1 and return 1.
